cards.title: Calculating with results
cards.body: Built-in functions give back values, so you can use them straight away in a calculation.

hi.title: Results ke saath calculate karna
hi.body: Built-in functions values wapas dete hain, isliye unhe seedhe calculation mein use kar sakte ho.

cards.title: Inside out
cards.body: Python works out `max(...)` and `min(...)` first, then applies the operator between their results.

hi.title: Andar se bahar
hi.body: Python pehle `max(...)` aur `min(...)` nikalta hai, phir unke results ke beech operator lagata hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the middle of the hottest and coldest days, `13.5`, but prints `22.5`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Division happens before addition, so only `min(temps)` is halved. Add brackets: `(max(temps) + min(temps)) / 2`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse sabse garam aur sabse thande din ka beech wala `13.5` print karna chahiye, par yeh `22.5` print karta hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Division addition se pehle hota hai, isliye sirf `min(temps)` aadha hota hai. Brackets lagao: `(max(temps) + min(temps)) / 2`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: max is 10 and min is 3, so 10 - 3 is 7.
